changes: Diagram A: noted that the email is trimmed and lowercased before lookup (Q7).
Diagram A: API builds the full link and the job carries {to, link}; worker only sends (Q1).
Diagram B: said how the token reaches the hidden field and leaves the URL bar (server fills field, page script uses history.replaceState) (Q2).
Failure paths: 'Changed' email line now covers enqueue failure and states the 302 still happens (Q5).
Notes: No enumeration marks same body/status as required and timing as a recommendation only (Q4).
Notes: Token in the queue now says the job carries the finished link and the queue must keep no payload after send or drop, replacing the vague 'delete the payload' (Q6).
Notes: added one line that normal login does not cancel an unexpired link (Q8).
Added an Open questions section at the end: breach list location, email uniqueness, queue payload retention (Q3, Q6, Q7).
POST /reset: stated the form sends only hidden T plus password, no login needed, token is the credential, and each retry restarts at step 1.
Burn UPDATE: showed RETURNING user_id as U and used U in the users UPDATE, so the source of U is explicit.
Step 4: said the changed email is a short fixed notice sent to users.email of U.
Request flow: marked the queue as separate from Postgres and the worker as an existing, unchanged, separate process; noted the client shows the 200 body.
DATA block: added that at most one live link per user exists at any time (answers what happens to other pending links).
Failure paths: added the COMMIT-fails-after-enqueue case and made the breach-lookup-down message explicit.
Open questions: added whether the worker polls or is pushed jobs.
Cut the 'Login does not cancel a link' note (the brief asks for nothing more)
Cut the open question about how the worker receives jobs (poll or push), since the design does not depend on it
Merged the two 'Known gap' notes (silent email failure and dropped 'password changed' email) into one
Shortened the 'Changed email fails' failure path, which repeated the gap note
Trimmed the Storage note to one sentence on where the token lives and why rows stay
Removed a repeated clause in the POST /reset aside about what the form sends
Kept the open questions together at the end
holes: Q3: Where does the breached-password list live? Is it a local file, a database table, or an external service? (author: Not known where the breached-password list lives; the brief only calls it 'the breached-password list'. The design needs only a yes/no lookup and fails closed if it is down. Added to Open questions.)

Q6: What does the worker do with the job payload on success, and what does 'delete the payload' mean for the queue you use? Who does it? (author: I do not know which queue technology is used or how it retains payloads. The design requirement is that no payload survives after send or drop, and that job bodies are not logged. Who enforces it (queue config or worker) needs confirming; added to Open questions.)

Q7: How is the email address matched to a user (case, whitespace)? What if two accounts could share an address? (author: Email is trimmed and lowercased before lookup (decided, stated in the diagram). Whether users.email is unique or stored lowercased is not known; the design assumes one user per normalised address. Added to Open questions.)

Q12: What is the 'worker' and how does it get triggered: does it poll the queue, or is it pushed jobs? Does it run as a separate process from the API server? (author: The worker is the existing email worker from the brief, and I assume it is a separate process. I do not know whether it polls or is pushed jobs. The design does not depend on it. Added to Open questions.)
